A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SageAttention, with matching main sections, equations, and experiments. All pages and substantive displays are readable. v2 ends with references; v3 adds Appendix A, which was included in the comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPU benchmarks, numerical-error measurements, model evaluations, and ablations in Figures 6–9 and Tables 1–11.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds LLaVA evaluations, quantization-method comparisons, numerical diagnostics, and additional timing and generation results.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 changes the stated adaptive selection rule: v2 allows SAGEAttn-vB or SAGEAttn-vT, whereas v3 tests SAGEAttn-vB, selects it above 99.8% cosine similarity, and otherwise uses SAGEAttn-B. The smoothing operation, quantizers, four available kernels, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation rerun.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 and Table 8 add visual question answering with LLaVA-1.6 on TextVQA, POPE, and VQAv2, extending the task coverage beyond language modeling, generation, and classification. Figure 11 also adds qualitative Open-Sora evaluation; v2 used Open-Sora prompts but did not evaluate that generator.

E2.justification: New Tables 13–15 evaluate AWQ on Llama2, Q-diffusion on Unidiffuser, and ViDiT-Q on CogvideoX, alongside the retained comparisons. Table 13 also includes AWQ combined with SageAttention. ViDiT-Q's quality scores are reported experimentally, while its speedup is explicitly a theoretical maximum.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify W4A16 AWQ and W8A8 diffusion comparators, a Torch-based implementation benchmark, per-token QK error measurements from Unidiffuser's 24th layer, and model-specific RTX3090 timings. Existing benchmark protocols are largely retained. Appendix A's newly stated COCO sample selection and kernel settings are disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: The appendix adds a composability test with AWQ, isolates QK precision under INT8 versus FP8 in Table 17, and measures attention-output error with and without K smoothing in Table 18. Figures 10–14 substantially expand qualitative case comparisons. These supplement the retained end-to-end smoothing, accumulator, and adaptive-quantization analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Additional tables retain point-estimate reporting; averages across layers and numerical approximation errors are not newly introduced uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing main-table values and kernel-speed curves are retained. Table 8 adds LLaVA accuracies of 60.09%, 86.44%, and 77.47%, versus full-precision 60.25%, 86.45%, and 77.55%. The appendix adds comparator scores, numerical errors, Torch timings, qualitative outputs, and RTX3090 speedups of 1.81x–5.38x. Table 13's Llama2 perplexities of 5.4721/5.4729 are separate results, not demonstrated improvements over Table 8's retained 5.823/5.824; the setting difference is unexplained.

T1.justification: Equation 2 corrects online-softmax rescaling from exp(current maximum minus previous maximum) to exp(previous maximum minus current maximum). Appendix A.5 adds a latency-based speedup-bound calculation. However, the newly stated terminal index j=bkv conflicts with Algorithm 1's block count Tn=N/bkv. The central smoothing identity remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: K smoothing, INT8 attention with FP16 accumulation, adaptive quantization, approximately 2.1x/2.7x acceleration over FlashAttention2/xformers, and negligible model-quality loss. Additional evaluations support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly attributes Llama2's quantization tolerance to relatively uniform Q, K, and V distributions and suggests controlling outliers to improve quantization. A.5 discusses complementarity with linear-layer quantization and its limited end-to-end acceleration potential. The existing Hopper implementation limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1–A.3 newly documents hardware, software versions, Q/K/V block sizes, warp/stage settings, the first 256 COCO 2014 validation annotations and corresponding images, prompt characteristics, and the TIMM checkpoint. This substantially expands reproduction information. Conversely, v3 removes the abstract's SageAttention code URL and adds a separate link for generation examples; removal of the URL does not establish code withdrawal.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for LLaVA-NeXT, TextVQA, POPE, VQAv2, and PyTorch documentation. Appendix A.5 newly positions SageAttention as complementary to AWQ, Q-diffusion, and ViDiT-Q. The main related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; ViDiT-Q was already cited in v2.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained, with localized grammatical edits and a rewritten adaptive-quantization paragraph. v3 adds a ten-subsection experimental appendix, but does not extensively rewrite or reorganize the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table 8 with a LLaVA panel and adds Tables 12–19 plus Figures 10–14, including parameter tables, comparisons, diagnostics, and substantial image/video galleries. Existing figures are largely retained with modest resizing and reflow. Table 7 also loses its explicit TOPS caption label.

improvement.justification: The reproduction details in A.1–A.3, additional task coverage, and targeted numerical diagnostics make v3 easier to assess and reproduce, while Equation 2 corrects a real mathematical error. These gains are qualified by unexplained Llama2 perplexity differences between Tables 13 and 8, theoretical rather than measured ViDiT-Q acceleration, the newly inconsistent terminal-index statement, and removal of the direct code link. The net improvement is useful but limited.
